- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) or neutral, model often underestimates; increase forecast baseline or add upward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction to prevent overreaction.
- When sentiment shifts from positive to negative (or vice versa), model lags in adjusting; introduce a 1–2 day lag correction to align with sentiment reversal.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of decline after peak), model often fails to recognize it; apply a “reversion buffer” to dampen upward forecasts.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overfit recent trends; use sentiment-weighted smoothing to reduce noise amplification.
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (e.g., alternating 0.33/1.00), model often misjudges direction; use sentiment average as a directional anchor.
